messages:
Devin: Heads-up 3 Acme incoming enterprise commit question. They've provided traffic: sustained chat ~420 qps (median convo ~28 tokens) and nightly embedding fanout bursts ~300 r/s for 30-45m. They want a reserved GPU commitment + burst/autoscale. Can we sketch ops + pricing?
Sasha: Quick read: chat is low-token high-concurrency pattern. Embeddings are heavy but can be batched. Do they need sub-250ms p95 for chat?
Devin: Yes, p95 target = 240ms. Embeddings can accept up to 2.5s. They also want BYOK KMS and 90d audit logs.
Kevin: Back-of-envelope perf: with our runtime and A100-equivalent, effective chat capacity ~45 qps/GPU (with batching & KV warm). So baseline GPUs = ceil(420/45)=10. Add AZ+failover + embedding headroom => recommend 13 reserved. Allow autoscale to 20 for embedding bursts.
Kevin: Optional path: run int8 quantized chat variant -> ~1.5x throughput => baseline drops to ~7 GPUs but risk of subtle quality regressions on some prompts.
Nina: From presales: customer cares about deterministic tail. If we pick H100, per-GPU throughput improves ~25-30% so reserved count could be 9-10, but rental rate higher.
Sasha: Proposal idea: give three options in quote:
- Safe: 13 reserved A100-equivalent, autoscale to 20, 12mo with 20% commit discount
- Lean: 7 reserved using quantized chat, autoscale to 14, 12mo with 27% discount + quality review clause
- Premium: 10 reserved H100, autoscale to 15, 12mo at 18% discount (higher price but fewer GPUs)
Maria: Security ops: BYOK KMS + SOC2 OK. Need to confirm whether customer's KMS is AWS KMS or external HSM; for cross-region failover we need key replication plan. I'll draft answers for the questionnaire.
Devin: Sales asked about burst billing control. Can we cap daily burst spend?
Kevin: Yes: implement burst credits plus throttle. Example policy: credits_per_gpu_per_day: 900s (15min) for peak bursts, chargeable overage alert but we can throttle once credits exhausted. Fallback model: small-chat-quantized at lower cost.
Kevin: Example autoscale snippet (YAML):
```
autoscale:
  baseline_reservation: 13
  max_scale: 20
  burst_credits_per_gpu_per_day: 900
  fallback:
    model: chat-small-quantized
    throttling: true
```
Nina: Ops preheat runbook suggestions: staged warm-up to populate KV cache + synthetic embedding batches to warm kernels. Stages: 1) 10% traffic 30m, 2) 50% traffic 1h, 3) full traffic. Use canary checks at each step.
Kevin: Preheat smoke command we use for warm cache: 
```
# run for 3600s at 1r/s per preheat client
for i in $(seq 1 3600); do
  curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":12}' >/dev/null || exit 1
  sleep 1
done
```
deploy-bot: preheat-smoke result: canary p95=230ms, p99=480ms, canary healthy :white_check_mark:
Sasha: Pricing ask: 6mo vs 12mo differences? Recommend listing both; 12mo better discount and committing to baseline. Also call out upgrade path if they want to switch to H100 mid-term (pricing true-up).
Maria: Action items: 1) @kevin produce numeric SKU quotes for A100 and H100 baselines + quantized variant by EOD. 2) @sasha draft dual-term pricing language (6/12mo) and explain upgrade/true-up mechanics. 3) @maria assemble SOC2 + BYOK answers for questionnaire and note any infra changes. 4) @devin request hourly spike traces from customer to refine burst model.
Devin: I'll ping the customer for traces and confirm KMS type. Thanks all, will reconvene after Kevin posts numbers.
